steps.determines: UNIQUE (the gradient fields are fixed by rho on the mesh)
steps.expr: for edge (u,v): rho(u)-rho(v); gm(v)=sum|rho(w)-rho(v)|; L(v)=sum(rho(w)-rho(v)); adjacency-only
steps.what: the density gradient: edge differences of rho, the per-vertex magnitude and the Laplacian
steps.why: gravity is the CHANGE in the packing, so the object is the GRADIENT of the density observable rho(v)=|B_r(v)| (container 13). Per edge (u,v): the difference rho(u)-rho(v). Per vertex: the gradient magnitude gm(v) = sum over neighbours |rho(w)-rho(v)|, and the graph Laplacian L(v) = sum (rho(w)-rho(v)). Both are pure adjacency -- no distance, no embedding -- exactly like |B_r| itself. At each of the twelve (a local minimum of rho) every neighbour is higher, so gm = L = 5r (five neighbours, each higher by r). Computed cold on R4 at r=3.

steps.why: the substrate realization of 'no change in packing -> no gravity'. Large regions have ZERO gradient -- rho is locally constant there, flat, no gravity: {'R3': '0/162', 'R4': '270/642', 'R5': '2190/2562'} (the flat fraction). steps.check: sum_v L(v) = 0 at every level (Gauss); rho(w)-rho(v) = deficit(v)-deficit(w) everywhere
steps.expr: sum_v L(v) = 0 exactly (each edge cancels); rho = flat - deficit so rho(w)-rho(v) = deficit(v)-deficit(w)
steps.what: the sources sum to zero (a discrete Gauss law), and grad(rho) = -grad(deficit)
steps.why: TWO exact facts. (a) THE GAUSS LAW: sum over all vertices of L(v) is 0 -- each edge (u,v) contributes rho(v)-rho(u) at u and rho(u)-rho(v) at v, which cancel. So the gravity SOURCES sum to zero on the CLOSED substrate (as total charge is zero on a closed universe): the twelve's positive sources are exactly balanced by the negative-L neighbours. Checked at every level: {'R3': 0, 'R4': 0, 'R5': 0}. (b) GRADIENT DUALITY: since rho = flat_ball(r) - deficit (14) and flat_ball is constant per r, grad(rho) = -grad(deficit) edge-by-edge -- the density gradient IS the negative of the curvature-deficit gradient. Gravity (grad rho) and curvature (deficit) are the same field, differentiated.
